title: Tech Note: Creating a 6.0-style Pop-up in 6.7 using Layered Objects
author: Eric Saltzen
featured_technology: Layered form objects (overlaying a display-only object on a Pop-up menu/Drop-down list)
POST CLICK command to forward clicks between layered objects
LIST TO ARRAY / Find in array for placeholder-based selection detection
On Load / On Clicked / On Getting Focus / On Losing Focus form events
SET RGB COLORS for Windows-style focus highlighting

historical_commentary.text: Eric Saltzen (4D, Inc. Technical Support) shows how to restore 4D v6.0's Pop-up menu/Drop-down list behavior — where the object method only fires on an actual user selection, not merely on browsing the menu — in v6.5+ (where Apple's Mac interface guidelines changed the firing behavior), by layering a placeholder-based list with a display-only overlay object and using POST CLICK to pass clicks through. This is a narrow interface-compatibility workaround for a one-time behavior change between two specific, decades-old 4D versions (6.0 to 6.5); the underlying layering/POST CLICK technique for combining form objects is still valid in principle, but the specific problem it solves is no longer relevant to any current 4D version, making the note itself obsolete while the general layering technique remains a still-usable pattern for advanced custom controls.
related_updates: The specific 4D v6.0-vs-6.5+ Pop-up/Drop-down list firing-behavior difference this note addresses is irrelevant to all current 4D versions
The general technique of layering form objects and using POST CLICK to forward clicks remains valid in current 4D versions for building custom composite controls
Modern 4D UI development (list boxes, plug-ins, or web-based front ends) rarely relies on hand-layered classic-language pop-up/drop-down workarounds
